chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Ayub ibn al-Hurr, from al-Harith the seller of silk fabrics, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about a man who bequeathed a Hajj [pilgrimage], so he said: 'If it is a single pilgrimage, it is taken from the main body of his wealth; for it is a debt upon him. But if he had already performed Hajj, it is taken from the one-third [share].'

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third share of the estate used for bequests
key_terms.صُلْبِ الْمَالِ: The main body of wealth (prior to deducting debts and one-third)

ai.seo_question: How is the cost of a bequeathed Hajj pilgrimage paid from an estate in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a bequeathed Hajj is treated as a debt against the estate, prioritized over the one-third bequest share, provided it is a voluntary (non-obligatory) Hajj. If the deceased had already fulfilled their obligatory Hajj, the bequeathed pilgrimage is funded from the one-third portion designated for bequests. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between obligatory and voluntary acts in estate distribution, emphasizing the precedence of Hajj debts over general bequests.
